text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Rebel-held town of Vlore greeted Italian troops with bouquets of flowers.

- An editorial calls on U.N.-backed 6,000 multinational force to maintain order during the elections due on June 29, saying only securing safety of humanitarian aid distribution is too little for such a strong force.
- Intelligence Secret Service (Shik) is still working despite a government decision to disband it, paper says.
- Exiled king Leka I had a warm and successful visit to his father's native village where he was welcomed by thousands of monarchy supporters.
- The budget deficit is expected to be some $500 million and inflation will go up to 55 percent this year, Finance Minister Arben Malaj is quoted as saying.
- Paper alleges former pyramid schemes managers, former members of the communist secret police and army officers are leading the rebel committees of public salvation in the south.
- Over 150,000 guns have been looted from military depots in southern town of Gramsh, where people are making a lot of money by selling Kalashnikovs, pistols and ammunition.
- After special police units left the town of Berat, criminal gangs retook control.
- Relations between President Sali Berisha and Prime Minister Bashkim Fino have been strained over the sacking of deputy interior minister and police chief Agim Shehu.
- Paper quotes Italian Corriere della Sera daily as saying some 700 Shik secret police officers are being trained in Feken area, near Tirana, allegedly to enforce Berisha's orders.
